title: When Noise Fabricates Bias: The Fragility of LLM-as-a-Judge Bias Measurement under Noisy Text
measurement_description: The paper evaluated how the presence of surface noise (such as typos, informal spelling, and missing punctuation) in text causes LLM-as-a-judge systems to falsely fabricate social bias. It measured the rate at which neutral texts are misjudged as biased across seven demographic categories, including religion.
findings: Religion was found to be the demographic category most vulnerable to noise-induced bias fabrication. Under combined surface noise at realistic intensities, the 'Religion' category experienced the highest rate of fabricated bias (10.2% conditional rate), indicating that LLM judges are most likely to hallucinate a biased judgment on neutral, unaligned texts about religion when surface noise is present.
